# Product composition (@nucleum/composition)

This workspace wires independently owned implementations into a running product.
It is not the default owner of connected components or workflows.

## Permanent owners

- root files: `configure-hosts.ts` registers hosts, `shortcuts.config.ts` supplies product shortcut defaults, `global-commands.ts` and `settings-actions.ts` assemble owner-defined actions, `SubAtomLogo.svelte` connects product identity to portable marks, and `AppLoadingView.svelte` and `ComponentResolver.svelte` connect startup and action presentation.
- layers: startup ordering, account access gating, connected user layout assembly, shell overlay mounting, product base layer wiring and telemetry consent/lifecycle wiring.
- chrome: product-connected snippets supplied to the independent shell, including native capture.

The root source files are an explicit allowlist in the architecture checker.
New root files or directories require an ownership decision and checker update.

## Responsibilities owned elsewhere

- shell/navigation and shell/layers: browser navigation, route decoding, route-driven layout, platform classes and viewport handling.
- shell/overlays and shell/modal: modal stacking, chrome and dismissal; composition registers the concrete action renderer and mounts the overlay layer.
- surfaces/settings and product settings owners: settings action definitions; composition preserves their final registry order.
- surfaces/library: mixed-resource rendering and bulk selection presentation; features/records owns record actions and bulk mutations.
- surfaces/account: OAuth, session hydration, extension login and environment-change sign-out.
- surfaces/subscription: plan reconciliation and native purchase outcomes.
- surfaces/settings/data-recovery: recovery decisions, UI, and DataFn import orchestration; persistence owns backup parsing and local storage mechanics.
- surfaces/settings/about: application-update workflow.
- surfaces/help: documentation, support, connected error recovery and shipped diagnostics.
- surfaces/sharing: permissions and public-link workflows.
- runtime: host detection, native message validation, service workers and log capture.
- shared-state/app-context, preferences and files: application metadata, timezone preferences and native file responses.
- ui/compositions: quick-access grids, hold-action presentation and point-map rendering.
- features/memory/maps: memory popup content and its map adapter.

Composition keeps lifecycle sequencing and supplies narrow callbacks to the
owning workflows. Do not move a large layer wholesale into another generic
controller, service, state or utilities directory. Do not add compatibility
re-exports at retired paths.

## Verification

Run npm run check:architecture, node tools/check/type-ownership.mjs, the product
compiler checks and relevant unit suites. Compiler/import success does not
prove browser, native purchase, legacy-data recovery or cloud behavior.

For the presentation-host and settings splits, manually verify account sign-in,
extension login, onboarding, branded loading, account navigation status,
library search and empty states, backup and restore, E2EE controls, and cache
actions on the Caddy HTTPS product hosts. Reopen settings and library surfaces
after writes to confirm persistent results.
# `client/shell` — application shell: arrangement and navigation (`@nucleum/shell`)

Charter: how the app is arranged and moved through, independent of what content
fills it. Pure "where things go and how you move", never "what a screen does".

## Owners

`navigation` (URL/history, resource navigation), `topNav`, `bottomNav`,
`leftPanel`, `rightPanel`, `trail`, `layers` (theme, metadata, embed),
`overlays`, `modal`, `paint` (page and
resource resolvers fed through the shared-state action renderer), `split views`,
`tabs`, `sync` and `notifications` chrome.

`navigation/NavigationLayout.svelte` owns route-driven arrangement and receives
connected nav snippets from application. `overlays/ModalLayer.svelte` owns the
overlay stack and resolves action content through the registered renderer.

## Belongs here

Anything that owns URL state, panel arrangement, tab/sidebar behavior, product
menus, or shell events. If removing it would not change what any single screen
does, only how screens are framed and reached, it belongs here.

## Not here

- Domain screens and workflows (account, library, settings, command) ->
  `surfaces/`.
- Portable domain-free UI -> `ui/`.
- Content capabilities -> `features/`.
- Sync scheduling -> `datafn/visibility-sync`; telemetry mechanics ->
  `runtime/telemetry`; consent/lifecycle wiring -> application layers;
  connected support -> `surfaces/help/support`.
- Application composition layers that wire the running product together
  (base/user layers, the action `ComponentResolver`, `AppLoadingView`, and the
  final settings action assembly) -> `application/`.

## Dependency direction (enforced)

Shell is acyclic: it must not import `application/`, `surfaces/`, or
`products/`, directly or transitively. Product navigation config enters through
`@nucleum/shared-state/product/product-config-host`; concrete chrome
(brand/logo, account avatar, search input, bulk-edit bar, offline status,
capture, profile section) enters through optional Svelte snippet props provided
by the application chrome adapters (`client/composition/chrome/`).

## Junk-drawer test

A shell component may read navigation and shell state, but it must not contain a
feature workflow. If it orchestrates a domain task (sign-in, billing, resource
browsing), it is a surface, not shell.
# `client/shared-state` — product-independent shared client state (`@nucleum/shared-state`)

Charter: reactive state and cross-cutting ports consumed across many features,
products, extensions, and the application shell. Not UI, not infrastructure, not
a single feature's state.

Named `shared-state`, **not** `capabilities`: user-facing capabilities are
`features/` (and product surfaces). This layer is the state they share.

## Owners (import named subpaths, no root barrel)

`app-context`, `appearance`, `commands`, `events`, `files`, `notifications`,
`preferences`, `product`, `resources`, `shortcuts`.

`events` owns the focus and memory event contracts; runtime extensions own
clipper transport events. `product` exposes the configured presentation host
consumed by surfaces without importing application composition.
`resources` owns headless resource state and host contracts; connected record
actions and bulk mutations live in `features/records`.

Example: `@nucleum/shared-state/preferences/preferences.store`.

## Belongs here

State or a contract that more than one feature/product needs and that has no UI
and no product-specific workflow. Concrete command *execution* stays in
application; the command *port* lives here because everyone consumes it.

## Never here (enforced)

Any import, direct or transitive, of `application`, `features`, or `products`.
May consume `runtime`, `datafn`, `persistence`, `schema`, `utils`, and portable
UI contracts only.

## Junk-drawer test

- Renders a screen? -> a `feature/` or product surface, not here.
- Pure infrastructure with no UI? -> `runtime/`.
- State owned by one feature? -> that feature.
- Do not add a generic `shared`, `core`, `state`, or `stores` bucket; file it
  under a named owner above.
# `client/runtime` — browser infrastructure, no UI

Charter: how the client talks to the outside world and computes, with no
presentation and no product workflow. It sits at the bottom and may be imported
by everyone, including extensions and workers that never load the full app.

## Owners

`account` (session state + transport), `audio`, `connectivity`, `embed`,
`inference`, `logging`, `os`, `context`.

## Belongs here

Transport, network authority, native/embed messaging, inference, audio decoding,
diagnostics, and the bare reactive state those need. Pure, low-dependency,
changes rarely.

## Never here (enforced)

Any import of `features`, `products`, `application`, the shell, `shared-state`,
or portable UI. Runtime is a leaf that others depend on, not the reverse.

## Junk-drawer test

- Has Svelte/DOM UI? -> not runtime.
- Coordinates a user-facing workflow (redirects, screens, prompts)? -> that
  workflow belongs in `application` or a feature; keep only the primitive here.
  (Example: `account.store` state lives here; the sign-in workflow does not.)
# `client/features` — user-facing content capabilities (`@nucleum/features`)

Charter: the marquee things a user creates and manages. Each feature is a
self-contained capability reached from outside only through declared entry
points.

## Owners

`calendar`, `collections`, `focus`, `memory`, `records`, `spaces`, `system`.

## Belongs here

A cohesive content capability with its own UI, state, and logic.
`records` owns connected record actions and bulk mutations; shared-state
supplies their headless selection state and application-configured host.

## Import rules (enforced)

- May import `ui`, `shared-state`, `runtime`, `datafn`, and the application
  **shell** surface only.
- May **not** import `products` or application workflows outside the shell.
- Cross-feature imports must target a path declared in
  `tools/check/feature-entrypoints.json`; there is no barrel.

## Junk-drawer test

If the thing operates *across* features or is *about the app itself* — account
and billing, the command palette, the resource library/browser, settings,
onboarding, help — it is a **product surface** and belongs in the top-level
`client/surfaces/` workspace (see `docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md`).
`features/` must never import `surfaces/`; the checker rejects that edge.
# `client/ui` — portable, domain-free presentation (`@21n/ui`)

Charter: reusable UI that knows nothing about this product. It must be droppable
into any product or extension unchanged.

## Layers (import direction is one-way, top depends on bottom)

- `compositions` — compound UI built from primitives (charts, maps, breadcrumbs,
  nested lists, search controls, file presentation, duration/time inputs).
- `elements` — atomic controls and UI-only types.
- `actions` — generic DOM behaviors.
- `icons`, `illustrations`, `branding` — portable visual assets.
- `environment` — package-wide portable platform state.
- `hosts` — dependency-inversion contracts for product behavior.

`compositions` may use every lower layer. `elements`, `actions`, `icons`,
`illustrations`, `branding`, `environment`, and `hosts` must never import
`compositions`.

## Belongs here

Presentation with credible cross-product reuse and **no** dependency on domain,
state, navigation, or infrastructure. A single current consumer is fine if reuse
is intended.

## Never here (enforced by `npm run check:architecture`)

Any import, direct or transitive, of `application`, the shell, `products`,
`features`, `datafn`, `persistence`, `schema`, `shared-state`, or `runtime`.

## Junk-drawer test

If it needs a store, navigation, a DataFn/domain type, or product branching, it
does **not** belong here. Feed those in through props or a `hosts` contract
configured by the owning application, shell, or feature layer.

# Legacy OAuth follow-up

Reviewed for PR #584 on 2026-09-14. This is an unresolved security risk, not a completed remediation or deployment verification.

## Evidence

- `client/application/account/oauth.ts` constructs state from guest and host values. URL encoding is present, but the state is predictable and is not a one-time browser-bound nonce.
- When configured for PKCE, that client sends the constant `challenge`. `server/common/oauth/oauth.utils.ts` sends the same constant as `code_verifier`.
- `server/common/oauth/oauth.ts` parses routing information directly from state. `server/common/oauth/oauth.endpoints.ts` owns the legacy callback redirection.
- `client/routes/embed/+page.svelte` still invokes this client flow. The ordinary account sign-in controls use `authClient().startSocialSignIn` instead.
- Legacy CDK code declares `oauth.handler`, but this review did not establish which deployed callback currently serves native clients. Source reachability does not prove deployment usage.

## Required follow-up

1. Inventory deployed callback URLs, provider configuration, and native app versions that invoke the embed flow.
2. Prefer migrating those callers to the account service's existing AuthFn social OAuth implementation. Verify provider support and native return routing before retiring legacy handlers.
3. If a legacy callback must remain, implement a matching initiation/callback transaction: cryptographically random single-use state, browser binding, expiry, replay prevention, provider binding, and validated redirect destinations. Generate a random PKCE verifier and S256 challenge and make the verifier available only to the matching token exchange.
4. Verify successful and rejected callbacks for Apple and Google, including native return handling, mismatched state, expired/replayed transactions, and incorrect verifiers.

Do not replace only the frontend state with a random value: the legacy callback currently depends on its guest/domain structure. Do not describe the runtime debug-host repair in PR #584 as a fix for state or PKCE security.

# Product composition (@nucleum/composition)

This workspace wires independently owned implementations into a running product.
It is not the default owner of connected components or workflows.

## Permanent owners

- root files: `configure-hosts.ts` registers hosts, `shortcuts.config.ts` supplies product shortcut defaults, `global-commands.ts` and `settings-actions.ts` assemble owner-defined actions, `SubAtomLogo.svelte` connects product identity to portable marks, and `AppLoadingView.svelte` and `ComponentResolver.svelte` connect startup and action presentation.
- layers: startup ordering, account access gating, connected user layout assembly, shell overlay mounting, product base layer wiring and telemetry consent/lifecycle wiring.
- chrome: product-connected snippets supplied to the independent shell, including native capture.

The root source files are an explicit allowlist in the architecture checker.
New root files or directories require an ownership decision and checker update.

## Responsibilities owned elsewhere

- shell/navigation and shell/layers: browser navigation, route decoding, route-driven layout, platform classes and viewport handling.
- shell/overlays and shell/modal: modal stacking, chrome and dismissal; composition registers the concrete action renderer and mounts the overlay layer.
- surfaces/settings and product settings owners: settings action definitions; composition preserves their final registry order.
- surfaces/library: mixed-resource rendering and bulk selection presentation; features/records owns record actions and bulk mutations.
- surfaces/account: OAuth, session hydration, extension login and environment-change sign-out.
- surfaces/subscription: plan reconciliation and native purchase outcomes.
- surfaces/settings/data-recovery: recovery decisions, UI, and DataFn import orchestration; persistence owns backup parsing and local storage mechanics.
- surfaces/settings/about: application-update workflow.
- surfaces/help: documentation, support, connected error recovery and shipped diagnostics.
- surfaces/sharing: permissions and public-link workflows.
- runtime: host detection, native message validation, service workers and log capture.
- shared-state/app-context, preferences and files: application metadata, timezone preferences and native file responses.
- ui/compositions: quick-access grids, hold-action presentation and point-map rendering.
- features/memory/maps: memory popup content and its map adapter.

Composition keeps lifecycle sequencing and supplies narrow callbacks to the
owning workflows. Do not move a large layer wholesale into another generic
controller, service, state or utilities directory. Do not add compatibility
re-exports at retired paths.

## Verification

Run npm run check:architecture, node tools/check/type-ownership.mjs, the product
compiler checks and relevant unit suites. Compiler/import success does not
prove browser, native purchase, legacy-data recovery or cloud behavior.

For the presentation-host and settings splits, manually verify account sign-in,
extension login, onboarding, branded loading, account navigation status,
library search and empty states, backup and restore, E2EE controls, and cache
actions on the Caddy HTTPS product hosts. Reopen settings and library surfaces
after writes to confirm persistent results.
# `client/shell` — application shell: arrangement and navigation (`@nucleum/shell`)

Charter: how the app is arranged and moved through, independent of what content
fills it. Pure "where things go and how you move", never "what a screen does".

## Owners

`navigation` (URL/history, resource navigation), `topNav`, `bottomNav`,
`leftPanel`, `rightPanel`, `trail`, `layers` (theme, metadata, embed),
`overlays`, `modal`, `paint` (page and
resource resolvers fed through the shared-state action renderer), `split views`,
`tabs`, `sync` and `notifications` chrome.

`navigation/NavigationLayout.svelte` owns route-driven arrangement and receives
connected nav snippets from application. `overlays/ModalLayer.svelte` owns the
overlay stack and resolves action content through the registered renderer.

## Belongs here

Anything that owns URL state, panel arrangement, tab/sidebar behavior, product
menus, or shell events. If removing it would not change what any single screen
does, only how screens are framed and reached, it belongs here.

## Not here

- Domain screens and workflows (account, library, settings, command) ->
  `surfaces/`.
- Portable domain-free UI -> `ui/`.
- Content capabilities -> `features/`.
- Sync scheduling -> `datafn/visibility-sync`; telemetry mechanics ->
  `runtime/telemetry`; consent/lifecycle wiring -> application layers;
  connected support -> `surfaces/help/support`.
- Application composition layers that wire the running product together
  (base/user layers, the action `ComponentResolver`, `AppLoadingView`, and the
  final settings action assembly) -> `application/`.

## Dependency direction (enforced)

Shell is acyclic: it must not import `application/`, `surfaces/`, or
`products/`, directly or transitively. Product navigation config enters through
`@nucleum/shared-state/product/product-config-host`; concrete chrome
(brand/logo, account avatar, search input, bulk-edit bar, offline status,
capture, profile section) enters through optional Svelte snippet props provided
by the application chrome adapters (`client/composition/chrome/`).

## Junk-drawer test

A shell component may read navigation and shell state, but it must not contain a
feature workflow. If it orchestrates a domain task (sign-in, billing, resource
browsing), it is a surface, not shell.
# `client/shared-state` — product-independent shared client state (`@nucleum/shared-state`)

Charter: reactive state and cross-cutting ports consumed across many features,
products, extensions, and the application shell. Not UI, not infrastructure, not
a single feature's state.

Named `shared-state`, **not** `capabilities`: user-facing capabilities are
`features/` (and product surfaces). This layer is the state they share.

## Owners (import named subpaths, no root barrel)

`app-context`, `appearance`, `commands`, `events`, `files`, `notifications`,
`preferences`, `product`, `resources`, `shortcuts`.

`events` owns the focus and memory event contracts; runtime extensions own
clipper transport events. `product` exposes the configured presentation host
consumed by surfaces without importing application composition.
`resources` owns headless resource state and host contracts; connected record
actions and bulk mutations live in `features/records`.

Example: `@nucleum/shared-state/preferences/preferences.store`.

## Belongs here

State or a contract that more than one feature/product needs and that has no UI
and no product-specific workflow. Concrete command *execution* stays in
application; the command *port* lives here because everyone consumes it.

## Never here (enforced)

Any import, direct or transitive, of `application`, `features`, or `products`.
May consume `runtime`, `datafn`, `persistence`, `schema`, `utils`, and portable
UI contracts only.

## Junk-drawer test

- Renders a screen? -> a `feature/` or product surface, not here.
- Pure infrastructure with no UI? -> `runtime/`.
- State owned by one feature? -> that feature.
- Do not add a generic `shared`, `core`, `state`, or `stores` bucket; file it
  under a named owner above.
# `client/runtime` — browser infrastructure, no UI

Charter: how the client talks to the outside world and computes, with no
presentation and no product workflow. It sits at the bottom and may be imported
by everyone, including extensions and workers that never load the full app.

## Owners

`account` (session state + transport), `audio`, `connectivity`, `embed`,
`inference`, `logging`, `os`, `context`.

## Belongs here

Transport, network authority, native/embed messaging, inference, audio decoding,
diagnostics, and the bare reactive state those need. Pure, low-dependency,
changes rarely.

## Never here (enforced)

Any import of `features`, `products`, `application`, the shell, `shared-state`,
or portable UI. Runtime is a leaf that others depend on, not the reverse.

## Junk-drawer test

- Has Svelte/DOM UI? -> not runtime.
- Coordinates a user-facing workflow (redirects, screens, prompts)? -> that
  workflow belongs in `application` or a feature; keep only the primitive here.
  (Example: `account.store` state lives here; the sign-in workflow does not.)
# `client/features` — user-facing content capabilities (`@nucleum/features`)

Charter: the marquee things a user creates and manages. Each feature is a
self-contained capability reached from outside only through declared entry
points.

## Owners

`calendar`, `collections`, `focus`, `memory`, `records`, `spaces`, `system`.

## Belongs here

A cohesive content capability with its own UI, state, and logic.
`records` owns connected record actions and bulk mutations; shared-state
supplies their headless selection state and application-configured host.

## Import rules (enforced)

- May import `ui`, `shared-state`, `runtime`, `datafn`, and the application
  **shell** surface only.
- May **not** import `products` or application workflows outside the shell.
- Cross-feature imports must target a path declared in
  `tools/check/feature-entrypoints.json`; there is no barrel.

## Junk-drawer test

If the thing operates *across* features or is *about the app itself* — account
and billing, the command palette, the resource library/browser, settings,
onboarding, help — it is a **product surface** and belongs in the top-level
`client/surfaces/` workspace (see `docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md`).
`features/` must never import `surfaces/`; the checker rejects that edge.
# `client/ui` — portable, domain-free presentation (`@21n/ui`)

Charter: reusable UI that knows nothing about this product. It must be droppable
into any product or extension unchanged.

## Layers (import direction is one-way, top depends on bottom)

- `compositions` — compound UI built from primitives (charts, maps, breadcrumbs,
  nested lists, search controls, file presentation, duration/time inputs).
- `elements` — atomic controls and UI-only types.
- `actions` — generic DOM behaviors.
- `icons`, `illustrations`, `branding` — portable visual assets.
- `environment` — package-wide portable platform state.
- `hosts` — dependency-inversion contracts for product behavior.

`compositions` may use every lower layer. `elements`, `actions`, `icons`,
`illustrations`, `branding`, `environment`, and `hosts` must never import
`compositions`.

## Belongs here

Presentation with credible cross-product reuse and **no** dependency on domain,
state, navigation, or infrastructure. A single current consumer is fine if reuse
is intended.

## Never here (enforced by `npm run check:architecture`)

Any import, direct or transitive, of `application`, the shell, `products`,
`features`, `datafn`, `persistence`, `schema`, `shared-state`, or `runtime`.

## Junk-drawer test

If it needs a store, navigation, a DataFn/domain type, or product branching, it
does **not** belong here. Feed those in through props or a `hosts` contract
configured by the owning application, shell, or feature layer.
26:`schema` owns resource definitions. `client/datafn` owns the client storage and sync runtime. `client/runtime` owns browser infrastructure such as account transport, network authority, connectivity, and diagnostic logging. `client/features` owns capability implementations. `client/products` composes those capabilities into product experiences. Client product identity composition lives in `client/config/product.type.ts`; cross-layer product identity lives in `schema/product.type.ts`; declarative navigation metadata lives in `client/config`.

# Legacy OAuth follow-up

Reviewed for PR #584 on 2026-09-14. This is an unresolved security risk, not a completed remediation or deployment verification.

## Evidence

- `client/application/account/oauth.ts` constructs state from guest and host values. URL encoding is present, but the state is predictable and is not a one-time browser-bound nonce.
- When configured for PKCE, that client sends the constant `challenge`. `server/common/oauth/oauth.utils.ts` sends the same constant as `code_verifier`.
- `server/common/oauth/oauth.ts` parses routing information directly from state. `server/common/oauth/oauth.endpoints.ts` owns the legacy callback redirection.
- `client/routes/embed/+page.svelte` still invokes this client flow. The ordinary account sign-in controls use `authClient().startSocialSignIn` instead.
- Legacy CDK code declares `oauth.handler`, but this review did not establish which deployed callback currently serves native clients. Source reachability does not prove deployment usage.

## Required follow-up

1. Inventory deployed callback URLs, provider configuration, and native app versions that invoke the embed flow.
2. Prefer migrating those callers to the account service's existing AuthFn social OAuth implementation. Verify provider support and native return routing before retiring legacy handlers.
3. If a legacy callback must remain, implement a matching initiation/callback transaction: cryptographically random single-use state, browser binding, expiry, replay prevention, provider binding, and validated redirect destinations. Generate a random PKCE verifier and S256 challenge and make the verifier available only to the matching token exchange.
4. Verify successful and rejected callbacks for Apple and Google, including native return handling, mismatched state, expired/replayed transactions, and incorrect verifiers.

Do not replace only the frontend state with a random value: the legacy callback currently depends on its guest/domain structure. Do not describe the runtime debug-host repair in PR #584 as a fix for state or PKCE security.

async function readGlobalEditMode(page: import("@playwright/test").Page) {
  return page.evaluate(

async function resetInteractionModeToDefault(
  page: import("@playwright/test").Page
) {
  await page.evaluate(
    async ({ modulePaths }) => {
      const { InteractionMode } = await import(modulePaths.interactionModePath);
      const { Action } = await import(modulePaths.actionEnumPath);
      const { uiState } = await import(modulePaths.uiStateStorePath);
      const { UIStateScope } = await import(modulePaths.uiStateTypePath);
      uiState.setState(Action.MODE_OF_INTERACTION, InteractionMode.DEFAULT, {
        scope: UIStateScope.PRODUCT
      });
    },
    {
      modulePaths: {
        actionEnumPath,
        interactionModePath,
        uiStateStorePath,
        uiStateTypePath
      }
    }
  );
  await page.reload({ waitUntil: "domcontentloaded" });
  await ensureInAppOnHome(page);
}

Focus and memory event contracts live under `client/shared-state/events`; clipper
transport events live under `client/runtime/extensions`. App metadata belongs to
`client/shared-state/app-context`. Surfaces consume application-selected action
rendering and product visuals through named shared-state hosts.

Presentation ownership is separate from navigation ownership. Neutral breadcrumbs and scroll containers live in UI. `client/shell/navigation/components/AppBreadcrumbs.svelte` translates application resource and path metadata into structural breadcrumb items and callbacks. Sidebars, tabs, split views, panels, and trails remain in the application shell when they own URL state, resource resolution, product menus, shell events, or other application orchestration. A component moves to UI only when its public contract can be expressed without product or domain vocabulary.

Application and extension shells configure permanent overlay, resource-action, panel, shortcut, recents, record-renderer, action-renderer, portable action, shortcut, file, environment, logging, and haptic contracts in `client/composition/configure-hosts.ts`. Configuration runs from base, user, and extension shells before presentation or command execution. Shell and feature adapters provide view-specific props such as keyboard matching, time scales, and address resolution. Shared Markdown display owns portable parsing; memory owns Markdown editing. Portable file presentation, resource enums, event contracts, and action identifiers no longer depend on capability implementations.

The public feature API is enumerated in `tools/check/feature-entrypoints.json`. Each has a static consumer outside its capability. The checker rejects unused public entries and private external imports. This reduces the previous 154 entries by moving shared contracts and infrastructure to their proper owners without introducing barrels or compatibility paths.

Registered workspaces declare their production source imports. `@nucleum/client` owns lower-level config and runtime; `@nucleum/shared-state` owns product-independent shared client behavior, application context, command ports, and events; `@nucleum/shell` owns the application shell; `@nucleum/surfaces` owns cross-feature product surfaces; `@21n/ui` owns all portable presentation and visual assets. Source workspaces bundled by an app declare co-hosted workspace requirements as peer dependencies; existing build dependencies remain dependencies. Peers describe the host's source compilation requirements without adding artificial Turbo build cycles. This is not a claim that each source package builds or installs independently. The checker verifies both resolved workspace and external package imports; test and story dependencies are outside this production-source check.

The narrow Library now mounts resource panes only after a resource is selected. A dedicated focus-capability test covers the portrait Library in Nucleum and Pointron; a seeded Recents probe verifies visibility before and after reload without page errors. Broader regression results are recorded below separately from the architecture checks.

## Application-state ownership follow-up

The portable viewport contract in `client/ui/environment` contains viewport and
presentation measurements only. Navigation state belongs to
`client/shared-state/app-context`. Settings resolves selected actions from the
`setting` URL parameter and the command host; thumbnails receive their active
state from the owning settings list.

To manually verify the settings state cleanup on each Caddy HTTPS product host,
open Settings and select Appearance, then Date & Time. Confirm the selected
entry and content heading match. Repeat at a constrained landscape viewport
(780 x 600) and portrait viewport (600 x 900), reload the selected setting,
and use browser Back to confirm selection and headings follow the URL. Run
`node apps/e2e-playwright/scripts/probe-library-recents.mjs` from the repository
root with the local Nucleum server running to verify Recents before and after
reload using its current shared-state module.

Product and application context lives in `client/shared-state/app-context/app.store.ts`. Browser/embed environment context lives in `client/runtime/context.store.ts`; persistent UI preference state lives in `client/shared-state/preferences/ui-state`; legacy product-key migration belongs to `client/persistence/migrations`. URL/history and resource navigation live in `client/shell/navigation/navigation.ts`. Product command lookup/execution lives in `client/surfaces/commands/action-runner.ts`; the permanent shared `CommandHost` contract lives in `client/shared-state/commands/command-host.ts` and is installed from `client/composition/configure-hosts.ts`. Application-wide events live in `client/shared-state/events`. No old methods delegate to the new owners.

Reactive account session state lives with the account runtime in `client/runtime/account/account.store.ts`. Authentication persistence, bootstrap, sign-in, sign-out, navigation, and DataFn teardown are coordinated by `client/surfaces/account/account-session.ts`. Deletion confirmation and cleanup orchestration live in `client/surfaces/account/account-deletion.ts`; subscription operations live in `client/surfaces/subscription/subscription.ts`; file conversion, thumbnail generation, signing, and local/remote storage live in `client/shared-state/files/file-upload.ts`. OAuth initiation and callback presentation belong to surfaces/account; legacy code exchange belongs to runtime/account.

The connected offline-status indicator lives in `client/composition/chrome`; shared elements and the shell do not read account session state. Application composition supplies the indicator to shell chrome.

Product menu persistence lives beside navigation. Tab and sidebar mutations live beside the application shell; generic UI-state persistence belongs to the preferences capability. Shortcut persistence, matching, hints, and the host contract live in `client/shared-state/shortcuts`; global shortcut execution lives in `client/shell/shortcuts`, and shortcut settings presentation lives in `client/surfaces/settings/shortcuts`. Headless notification state lives in `client/shared-state/notifications`, while connected notification rendering lives in `client/shell/notifications`. Focus owns its scheduled notification queue, and the existing native transport delivers messages. Memory owns its word-count and PDF-overlay DOM actions. The unused Markdown action and empty `@nucleum/cx` workspace are retired, including active aliases and workspace declarations.

The former `client/stores`, `client/state`, `client/commands`, and `client/events` directories are retired. App context, appearance, commands, events, files, notifications, preferences, resources, and shortcuts have explicit owners under `client/shared-state`. Runtime environment state belongs to runtime, migration state belongs to persistence, the observable-store implementation belongs to DataFn, and overlay state belongs to the application shell. New state follows semantic ownership and must not recreate a catch-all `stores`, `state`, `shared`, or `core` directory; `client/shared-state` is the single approved shared-state workspace and keeps named owners with no root barrel.

Connected record menus and bulk mutations live in `client/features/records`; shared-state/resources retains selection state and the resource action host contract. DataFn resource selection, storage lifecycle, runtime policy and remote transport have named modules; `datafn.store.ts` owns the live client and lifecycle. Persistence separates client storage, device identity, legacy local storage, and the named legacy-backup operations. URL validation and product host parsing have named cross-layer utilities; memory owns its embed sanitizer, and the legacy Surreal query builder lives with server sync.

## Application composition refinement

`client/utils` and `@21n/utils` are retired, including their workspace and aliases.
Date arithmetic, parsing, period contracts, timezone lookup, user-date calculation
and file-size conversion are domain-free named modules under `shared/utils`.
Duration presentation belongs to UI time controls, chart formatting to chart
compositions, contextual events to UI environment, and color presentation to
theme. Focus owns session-item ordering; shell owns the existing touch-navigation
behavior. Extension transport lives in runtime/extensions, extension navigation

Authentication persistence, bootstrap, sign-in, sign-out, navigation, and DataFn teardown are coordinated by `client/surfaces/account/account-session.ts`. Deletion confirmation and cleanup orchestration live in `client/surfaces/account/account-deletion.ts`; subscription operations live in `client/surfaces/subscription/subscription.ts`; file conversion, thumbnail generation, signing, and local/remote storage live in `client/shared-state/files/file-upload.ts`. OAuth initiation and callback presentation belong to surfaces/account; legacy code exchange belongs to runtime/account.

The connected offline-status indicator lives in `client/composition/chrome`; shared elements and the shell do not read account session state. Application composition supplies the indicator to shell chrome.

Product menu persistence lives beside navigation. Tab and sidebar mutations live beside the application shell; generic UI-state persistence belongs to the preferences capability. Shortcut persistence, matching, hints, and the host contract live in `client/shared-state/shortcuts`; global shortcut execution lives in `client/shell/shortcuts`, and shortcut settings presentation lives in `client/surfaces/settings/shortcuts`. Headless notification state lives in `client/shared-state/notifications`, while connected notification rendering lives in `client/shell/notifications`. Focus owns its scheduled notification queue, and the existing native transport delivers messages. Memory owns its word-count and PDF-overlay DOM actions. The unused Markdown action and empty `@nucleum/cx` workspace are retired, including active aliases and workspace declarations.

The former `client/stores`, `client/state`, `client/commands`, and `client/events` directories are retired. App context, appearance, commands, events, files, notifications, preferences, resources, and shortcuts have explicit owners under `client/shared-state`. Runtime environment state belongs to runtime, migration state belongs to persistence, the observable-store implementation belongs to DataFn, and overlay state belongs to the application shell. New state follows semantic ownership and must not recreate a catch-all `stores`, `state`, `shared`, or `core` directory; `client/shared-state` is the single approved shared-state workspace and keeps named owners with no root barrel.

Connected record menus and bulk mutations live in `client/features/records`; shared-state/resources retains selection state and the resource action host contract. DataFn resource selection, storage lifecycle, runtime policy and remote transport have named modules; `datafn.store.ts` owns the live client and lifecycle. Persistence separates client storage, device identity, legacy local storage, and the named legacy-backup operations. URL validation and product host parsing have named cross-layer utilities; memory owns its embed sanitizer, and the legacy Surreal query builder lives with server sync.

compositions, contextual events to UI environment, and color presentation to
theme. Focus owns session-item ordering; shell owns the existing touch-navigation

109	The narrow Library now mounts resource panes only after a resource is selected. A dedicated focus-capability test covers the portrait Library in Nucleum and Pointron; a seeded Recents probe verifies visibility before and after reload without page errors. Broader regression results are recorded below separately from the architecture checks.
   110	
   111	## Application-state ownership follow-up
   112	
   113	The portable viewport contract in `client/ui/environment` contains viewport and
   114	presentation measurements only. Navigation state belongs to
   115	`client/shared-state/app-context`. Settings resolves selected actions from the
   116	`setting` URL parameter and the command host; thumbnails receive their active
   117	state from the owning settings list.
   118	
   119	To manually verify the settings state cleanup on each Caddy HTTPS product host,
   120	open the Settings page (`/cp`) and select Appearance, then Date & Time. Confirm
   121	the selected entry and content heading match. Repeat after reopening Settings
   122	at a constrained landscape viewport (780 x 600) and portrait viewport
   123	(600 x 900), then reload the selected setting. Orientation changes navigate
   124	to the product home, and setting selection replaces the current history entry.
   125	Run
   126	`node apps/e2e-playwright/scripts/probe-library-recents.mjs` from the repository
   127	root with the local Nucleum server running to verify Recents before and after
   128	reload using its current shared-state module.
   129	
   130	The 2026-10-03 cleanup passes architecture, type ownership, configured lint,
   131	legacy-runtime and fixed-wait checks, all four product compilers, 405 client and
   132	shared unit tests, and frontend deployment configuration validation. Explicit
   133	negative controls reject compositions imports from all seven lower UI layers.
   134	Nucleum offline browser checks verify Settings page selection at 780 x 600,
   135	headings at 600 x 900, reload at both sizes, and Recents visibility
   136	before and after reload. These checks use a temporary Caddy HTTPS proxy,
   137	browser-only hostname overrides, and HTTP/1.1 to avoid local upstream connection
   138	resets under concurrent HTTP/2 module requests. At constrained landscape widths,
   139	the shell Panel suppresses its right-hand content, so the selected section's
   140	content heading cannot be verified in that layout. The root Settings modal smoke
   141	dismisses the overlay on setting-query navigation. These separate shell workflow
   142	gaps remain outside this cleanup. Live account auth/sync, other products'
   143	browser workflows, native packaging, and production deployment were not tested.
   144	
   145	Product and application context lives in `client/shared-state/app-context/app.store.ts`. Browser/embed environment context lives in `client/runtime/context.store.ts`; persistent UI preference state lives in `client/shared-state/preferences/ui-state`; legacy product-key migration belongs to `client/persistence/migrations`. URL/history and resource navigation live in `client/shell/navigation/navigation.ts`. Product command lookup/execution lives in `client/surfaces/commands/action-runner.ts`; the permanent shared `CommandHost` contract lives in `client/shared-state/commands/command-host.ts` and is installed from `client/composition/configure-hosts.ts`. Application-wide events live in `client/shared-state/events`. No old methods delegate to the new owners.
   146	
   147	Reactive account session state lives with the account runtime in `client/runtime/account/account.store.ts`. Authentication persistence, bootstrap, sign-in, sign-out, navigation, and DataFn teardown are coordinated by `client/surfaces/account/account-session.ts`. Deletion confirmation and cleanup orchestration live in `client/surfaces/account/account-deletion.ts`; subscription operations live in `client/surfaces/subscription/subscription.ts`; file conversion, thumbnail generation, signing, and local/remote storage live in `client/shared-state/files/file-upload.ts`. OAuth initiation and callback presentation belong to surfaces/account; legacy code exchange belongs to runtime/account.
   148	
   149	The connected offline-status indicator lives in `client/composition/chrome`; shared elements and the shell do not read account session state. Application composition supplies the indicator to shell chrome.
   150	
Removed the temporary Caddy configuration and certificates created for QA.

# Client ownership and import boundaries

Current ownership contract for the client. If this file disagrees with `tools/check/client-dependency-matrix.json` or `npm run check:architecture`, the checker wins. Update this file in the same change that moves an owner or an allowed edge.

Diagrams and the direct-import matrix live in [client dependency map](client-dependency-map.md). Type placement lives in [type ownership](type-ownership.md). The TIDY-477 phase journal lives in [history/tidy-477-client-boundaries.md](history/tidy-477-client-boundaries.md).

## Ownership

| Owner | Owns |
| --- | --- |
| `schema` | Resource definitions, cross-layer product identity (`schema/product.type.ts`), and billing wire contracts (`schema/account`). |
| `client/config` | Client product identity, action identifiers, and declarative navigation metadata. |
| `client/datafn` | Client storage, the sync runtime, visibility sync, and the live DataFn client in `datafn.store.ts`. |
| `client/runtime` | Account transport and session state, network authority, connectivity, logging, browser and embed context, service-worker registration, native messages, inference, and telemetry SDK mechanics. |
| `client/persistence` | Client storage, device identity, legacy local storage, migrations, and legacy backup. The logger arrives through `persistence/logging-host`. |
| `client/ui` | Domain-free portable presentation (`@21n/ui`). See the UI layers below. |
| `client/shared-state` | Product-independent client behavior under the named owners below. No root barrel. |
| `client/shell` | Navigation, panels, split views, tabs, trails, overlays, modal chrome, connected notification rendering, and global shortcut execution (`@nucleum/shell`). |
| `client/features` | Capability implementations. Memory owns Markdown editing and tags. Spaces owns combinations. Records owns connected record menus and bulk mutations. Focus owns its scheduled notification queue. |
| `client/surfaces` | Cross-feature product surfaces: account, subscription, onboarding, help, settings, the command surface, search, and library (`@nucleum/surfaces`). |
| `client/products` | Product experiences composed from those capabilities. Product source does not import composition. |
| `client/composition` | The composition root, `layers/`, and `chrome/`: host installation, base and user layers, command-registry assembly, and product-aware branding adapters (`@nucleum/composition`). |
| `client/routes` | The shared SvelteKit route tree for Nucleum, Memotron, and Pointron. |
| `apps/` | Thin product hosts. `apps/<product>/src/local.ts` selects that product's base layer. Timear keeps its own routes. |

`client/ui` layers:

| Layer | Owns |
| --- | --- |
| `elements` | Atomic controls and UI-only types. Keyboard and interaction-mode contracts live in `elements/keyboard`. |
| `compositions` | Domain-neutral compound UI, including charts, maps, breadcrumbs, nested lists, search controls, file presentation, keyboard listeners, duration inputs, scroll containers, and time selectors. |
| `actions` | Generic DOM behavior. Capability-specific actions stay beside their consumer. |
| `icons`, `illustrations`, `branding` | Portable icons, artwork, and pure visual marks. |
| `environment` | Portable viewport and presentation measurements. |
| `hosts` | Dependency-inversion contracts shared by controls and compositions. |

`client/shared-state` owners: `app-context`, `appearance`, `commands`, `events`, `files`, `notifications`, `preferences`, `product`, `resources`, `shortcuts`. Import a named subpath such as `@nucleum/shared-state/preferences/preferences.store`.

State that looks shared but has a narrower owner:

| Concern | Owner |
| --- | --- |
| Browser and embed environment | `client/runtime/context.store.ts` |
| Account session state | `client/runtime/account/account.store.ts` |
| Sign-in, sign-out, bootstrap, and DataFn teardown | `client/surfaces/account/account-session.ts` |
| Account deletion | `client/surfaces/account/account-deletion.ts` |
| Subscription operations | `client/surfaces/subscription` |
| File upload, conversion, and storage | `client/shared-state/files` |
| URL and resource navigation | `client/shell/navigation/navigation.ts` |
| Command lookup and execution | `client/surfaces/commands/action-runner.ts` |
| Command definitions | The feature, surface, shell, or product that owns the action. `client/composition/global-commands.ts` only preserves assembly order. |
| Headless notifications | `client/shared-state/notifications` |
| Connected notification rendering | `client/shell/notifications` |
| Shortcut persistence and matching | `client/shared-state/shortcuts` |
| Global shortcut execution | `client/shell/shortcuts` |
| Shortcut settings | `client/surfaces/settings/shortcuts` |
| Selection state and the resource-action host | `client/shared-state/resources` |
| Support integration | `client/surfaces/help/support`, mounted by composition |
| Diagnostics and error screens | `client/surfaces/help` |
| Legacy recovery presentation | `client/surfaces/settings/data-recovery` |

## Closed edges

`npm run check:architecture` enforces the matrix in `tools/check/client-dependency-matrix.json`, including type-only imports. These are the edges that are easy to miss from the matrix alone:

- Features do not import products, surfaces, or composition. Shell is the only app-level layer they may use. Surfaces may compose features.
- Surfaces do not import composition. Product fields arrive through `@nucleum/shared-state/product/surface-config-host`.
- Shell does not import composition, surfaces, or products, directly or transitively. Product navigation arrives through `@nucleum/shared-state/product/product-config-host`.
- Shared-state does not import composition, features, or products, directly or transitively, including through type-only imports.
- DataFn and runtime do not import features, products, composition, shell, UI, or shared-state.
- UI does not import application state, runtime, shell, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, or domain state, directly or transitively.
- Inside UI, compositions may use elements, actions, icons, illustrations, branding, environment, and hosts. Those lower layers do not import compositions.
- Composition calculations do not import the session singleton.
- A caller outside a capability uses a source file listed in `tools/check/feature-entrypoints.json`. That list is the public surface, not a barrel. Additions are an explicit contract change. Package exports expose the same paths.

Tests and stories are outside the production-source import gate. `client/ui` is one matrix owner; the lower-layer rule above is separate. The aggregate `client/package.json` is not a matrix owner.

## Hosts

Lower layers do not import composition to reach product behavior. `client/composition/configure-hosts.ts` runs from the base, user, and extension shells before presentation or command execution.

| Contract | Installed by | Read by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Command, action renderer, overlay, resource action, resource panel, record renderer, recents, shortcut, and product-presentation hosts | `configure-hosts.ts` | Shell, features, and surfaces |
| `@21n/ui/hosts` and `@21n/ui/environment` | `configure-hosts.ts`, or the owning shell or feature adapter | Portable UI |
| `product-config-host` | Composition | Shell |
| `surface-config-host` | Composition | Surfaces |
| Chrome snippets (brand, search, bulk edit, offline status, capture, profile) | `client/composition/chrome/` | Shell, through optional snippet props |
| `persistence/logging-host` | Composition | Persistence |

Shell and feature adapters pass view-specific props such as keyboard matching, time scales, and address resolution. Do not add a compatibility wrapper or a generic service locator.

## Placement rules

These rules are semantic. The import checker does not decide them.

- A single current consumer does not make a composition feature-owned. Keep a domain-neutral composition in `client/ui/compositions` when future reuse is intentional.
- A component moves to UI only when its public contract can be expressed without product or domain vocabulary. Neutral breadcrumbs and scroll containers live in UI. `client/shell/navigation/components/AppBreadcrumbs.svelte` turns resource and path metadata into those items. Sidebars, tabs, split views, panels, and trails stay in the shell while they own URL state, resource resolution, or product menus.
- Product-aware branding that reads persistence or account identity stays in a named composition adapter, such as `client/composition/SubAtomLogo.svelte`, and composes portable marks through props.
- Shared Markdown display owns portable parsing. Memory owns Markdown editing.
- Account runtime state does not own file processing, deletion confirmation, or subscription workflows.
- Do not recreate `client/utils`, `client/stores`, `client/state`, `client/commands`, `client/events`, `client/layout`, `client/branding`, `client/illustrations`, `client/icons`, `client/iconsV2`, or `client/application`. Do not add a catch-all `stores`, `state`, `shared`, or `core` directory.
- When moving a module, update callers, feature exports, dependency declarations, and type-inventory destinations directly. Do not leave a compatibility re-export.

| `client/routes` | The shared SvelteKit route tree for Nucleum, Memotron, and Pointron. |
| `apps/` | Thin product hosts. `apps/<product>/src/local.ts` selects that product's base layer. Timear keeps its own routes. |

| Layer | Owns |
| --- | --- |
| `elements` | Atomic controls and UI-only types. Keyboard and interaction-mode contracts live in `elements/keyboard`. |
| `compositions` | Domain-neutral compound UI, including charts, maps, breadcrumbs, nested lists, search controls, file presentation, keyboard listeners, duration inputs, scroll containers, and time selectors. |

| `icons`, `illustrations`, `branding` | Portable icons, artwork, and pure visual marks. |
| `environment` | Portable viewport and presentation measurements. |
| `hosts` | Dependency-inversion contracts shared by controls and compositions. |

| Connected notification rendering | `client/shell/notifications` |
| Shortcut persistence and matching | `client/shared-state/shortcuts` |
| Global shortcut execution | `client/shell/shortcuts` |
| Shortcut settings | `client/surfaces/settings/shortcuts` |
| Selection state and the resource-action host | `client/shared-state/resources` |
| Support integration | `client/surfaces/help/support`, mounted by composition |
| Diagnostics and error screens | `client/surfaces/help` |
| Legacy recovery presentation | `client/surfaces/settings/data-recovery` |

`npm run check:architecture` enforces the matrix in `tools/check/client-dependency-matrix.json`, including type-only imports. These are the edges that are easy to miss from the matrix alone:

- Features do not import products, surfaces, or composition. Shell is the only app-level layer they may use. Surfaces may compose features.
- Surfaces do not import composition. Product fields arrive through `@nucleum/shared-state/product/surface-config-host`.
- Shell does not import composition, surfaces, or products, directly or transitively. Product navigation arrives through `@nucleum/shared-state/product/product-config-host`.
- Shared-state does not import composition, features, or products, directly or transitively, including through type-only imports.
- DataFn and runtime do not import features, products, composition, shell, UI, or shared-state.
- UI does not import application state, runtime, shell, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, or domain state, directly or transitively.

- Composition calculations do not import the session singleton.

| --- | --- | --- |

These rules are semantic. The import checker does not decide them.

- A single current consumer does not make a composition feature-owned. Keep a domain-neutral composition in `client/ui/compositions` when future reuse is intentional.

# Type and contract ownership

Current type-placement contract. If this file disagrees with `docs/architecture/type-ownership-inventory.json` or `node tools/check/type-ownership.mjs`, the checker wins. Update the inventory in the same change that moves a type module.

Application, navigation, account, file, and command ownership lives in [client boundaries](client-boundaries.md). The TIDY-478 phase journal lives in [history/tidy-478-type-ownership.md](history/tidy-478-type-ownership.md).

## Conventions

Definitions stay beside their implementation unless independent consumers need a neutral contract. Feature contracts belong to the feature, and external callers use the public entries in `tools/check/feature-entrypoints.json`.

Portable UI controls own their structural prop and style types:

| Contract | Owner |
| --- | --- |
| Primitive prop and style types | `client/ui/elements` |
| Domain-neutral composition contracts | `client/ui/compositions` |
| Generic DOM-action contracts | `client/ui/actions` |
| Package-wide host contracts | `client/ui/hosts` |
| Portable platform state | `client/ui/environment` |
| Visual asset contracts | `client/ui/icons`, `client/ui/illustrations`, or `client/ui/branding` |

Those UI contracts do not derive from schema records, DataFn resources, runtime types, application actions, or state interfaces. Owning adapters translate domain models at the UI boundary.

| Contract | Owner |
| --- | --- |
| Keyboard and interaction mode | `client/ui/elements/keyboard` |
| Application action identifiers | `client/config` |
| Command host | `client/shared-state/commands` |
| Application events | `client/shared-state/events`. Focus and memory events live here. Clipper transport events live in `client/runtime/extensions`. |
| Resource panel and selection | `client/shared-state/resources` |
| Headless notification state | `client/shared-state/notifications` |
| Connected notification rendering | `client/shell/notifications` |
| Error recovery screens | `client/surfaces/help/errors` |
| Product menu contracts | `client/shell/navigation/app-menu.type.ts` |
| Browser ambient declarations | `client/ambient` |
| Cross-layer account, subscription, and legacy wire contracts | `schema` |
| Generated AuthFn and DataFn/Drizzle files | `services/account` generation scripts. Do not edit them by hand. |

`schema/account` owns profile and subscription wire data. Billing presentation fields stay in `client/surfaces/subscription`. `schema/legacy` owns the existing Surreal mutation, query, sync, resource-action, and store-data encodings. Do not derive those legacy shapes from current DataFn records. `schema/datafn.ts` derives resource names from `nucleumDatafnSchema`. Client `Resource`, `MetaResource`, and `Product` compose schema values with the Next overlay; backend callers import schema directly.

Generic error codes are schema-owned. The default error message belongs to `client/shared-state/notifications`. Markdown validation belongs to memory. Responsive text truncation belongs to the text primitive. The legacy relay request contract lives in `server/common/relay/relay.type.ts` and imports only schema-owned resource and query contracts.

Native transcription model identifiers and worker model identifiers are different protocols. Both live in `client/runtime/inference`, in separate modules, with their original enum values.

The global `client/types` and `shared/types` packages are retired. Do not replace them with a catch-all types package or a compatibility export. Splits use a direct import to the actual owner.

## Import and export rules

Import interfaces and aliases with `import type` or a named `type` specifier. A runtime enum stays a value import. Do not re-export a moved definition from its former location. Public feature entries in `tools/check/feature-entrypoints.json` match the feature package exports. DataFn and schema expose their contracts directly.

`npm run check:architecture` checks static imports, exports, dynamic imports, import types, CommonJS requires, and Vitest mock imports. It rejects production schema, shared, server, and service imports into client code, rejects every server-to-client import, and rejects retired package aliases. Historical specs and append-only `.conduct` reports may still name the old layout. Active guidance and configuration use the current owners.

`node tools/check/type-ownership.mjs` checks every recorded destination in [type-ownership-inventory.json](type-ownership-inventory.json) and compares runtime enum declarations to that baseline. One audited retirement is recorded there: the disconnected shell cache `CacheKey` enum. No other runtime-enum retirement is exempt.

# Product composition (@nucleum/composition)

This workspace wires independently owned implementations into a running product.
It is not the default owner of connected components or workflows.

## Permanent owners

- root files: `configure-hosts.ts` registers hosts, `shortcuts.config.ts` supplies product shortcut defaults, `global-commands.ts` and `settings-actions.ts` assemble owner-defined actions, `SubAtomLogo.svelte` connects product identity to portable marks, and `AppLoadingView.svelte` and `ComponentResolver.svelte` connect startup and action presentation.
- layers: startup ordering, account access gating, connected user layout assembly, shell overlay mounting, product base layer wiring and telemetry consent/lifecycle wiring.
- chrome: product-connected snippets supplied to the independent shell, including native capture.

The root source files are an explicit allowlist in the architecture checker.
New root files or directories require an ownership decision and checker update.

## Responsibilities owned elsewhere

- shell/navigation and shell/layers: browser navigation, route decoding, route-driven layout, platform classes and viewport handling.
- shell/overlays and shell/modal: modal stacking, chrome and dismissal; composition registers the concrete action renderer and mounts the overlay layer.
- surfaces/settings and product settings owners: settings action definitions; composition preserves their final registry order.
- surfaces/library: mixed-resource rendering and bulk selection presentation; features/records owns record actions and bulk mutations.
- surfaces/account: OAuth, session hydration, extension login and environment-change sign-out.
- surfaces/subscription: plan reconciliation and native purchase outcomes.
- surfaces/settings/data-recovery: recovery decisions, UI, and DataFn import orchestration; persistence owns backup parsing and local storage mechanics.
- surfaces/settings/about: application-update workflow.
- surfaces/help: documentation, support, connected error recovery and shipped diagnostics.
- surfaces/sharing: permissions and public-link workflows.
- runtime: host detection, native message validation, service workers and log capture.
- shared-state/app-context, preferences and files: application metadata, timezone preferences and native file responses.
- ui/compositions: quick-access grids, hold-action presentation and point-map rendering.
- features/memory/maps: memory popup content and its map adapter.

Composition keeps lifecycle sequencing and supplies narrow callbacks to the
owning workflows. Do not move a large layer wholesale into another generic
controller, service, state or utilities directory. Do not add compatibility
re-exports at retired paths.

## Verification

Run npm run check:architecture, node tools/check/type-ownership.mjs, the product
compiler checks and relevant unit suites. Compiler/import success does not
prove browser, native purchase, legacy-data recovery or cloud behavior.

For the presentation-host and settings splits, manually verify account sign-in,
extension login, onboarding, branded loading, account navigation status,
library search and empty states, backup and restore, E2EE controls, and cache
actions on the Caddy HTTPS product hosts. Reopen settings and library surfaces
after writes to confirm persistent results.
# `client/shell` — application shell: arrangement and navigation (`@nucleum/shell`)

Charter: how the app is arranged and moved through, independent of what content
fills it. Pure "where things go and how you move", never "what a screen does".

## Owners

`navigation` (URL/history, resource navigation), `topNav`, `bottomNav`,
`leftPanel`, `rightPanel`, `trail`, `layers` (theme, metadata, embed),
`overlays`, `modal`, `paint` (page and
resource resolvers fed through the shared-state action renderer), `split views`,
`tabs`, `sync` and `notifications` chrome.

`navigation/NavigationLayout.svelte` owns route-driven arrangement and receives
connected nav snippets from application. `overlays/ModalLayer.svelte` owns the
overlay stack and resolves action content through the registered renderer.

## Belongs here

Anything that owns URL state, panel arrangement, tab/sidebar behavior, product
menus, or shell events. If removing it would not change what any single screen
does, only how screens are framed and reached, it belongs here.

## Not here

- Domain screens and workflows (account, library, settings, command) ->
  `surfaces/`.
- Portable domain-free UI -> `ui/`.
- Content capabilities -> `features/`.
- Sync scheduling -> `datafn/visibility-sync`; telemetry mechanics ->
  `runtime/telemetry`; consent/lifecycle wiring -> application layers;
  connected support -> `surfaces/help/support`.
- Application composition layers that wire the running product together
  (base/user layers, the action `ComponentResolver`, `AppLoadingView`, and the
  final settings action assembly) -> `composition/`.

## Dependency direction (enforced)

Shell is acyclic: it must not import `composition/`, `surfaces/`, or
`products/`, directly or transitively. Product navigation config enters through
`@nucleum/shared-state/product/product-config-host`; concrete chrome
(brand/logo, account avatar, search input, bulk-edit bar, offline status,
capture, profile section) enters through optional Svelte snippet props provided
by the application chrome adapters (`client/composition/chrome/`).

## Junk-drawer test

A shell component may read navigation and shell state, but it must not contain a
feature workflow. If it orchestrates a domain task (sign-in, billing, resource
browsing), it is a surface, not shell.
# `client/surfaces` — cross-feature product surfaces (`@nucleum/surfaces`)

Charter: user-facing surfaces that are about the app itself or operate across
all content features. Second-order UI: it composes `features/`, `shell/`, and
shared state into product-level experiences.

## Owners

`account` (identity workflows), `subscription` (billing and native purchases), `onboarding`, `help` (docs, support, error recovery and shipped diagnostics),
`settings` (including data recovery), `sharing`, `commandBar` + `commands` + `search` (command surface), `library`
(resource browsing and rendering).
Settings defines its action descriptors; product-specific settings define theirs
under the owning product. Application composes the final registry order.

## Why not `features/`

Features are first-order content capabilities a user creates and manages
(memory, focus, collections, spaces, calendar). Surfaces are about the product:
identity, billing, settings, command dispatch, and browsing every resource type.

## Import rules (enforced)

- May import `features`, `shell`, `shared-state`, `runtime`, `datafn`, `ui`,
  and `persistence`. Product fields and application-selected presentation enter
  through narrow shared-state hosts configured before surfaces mount.
- Must not import `products` or `composition`; these owners assemble surfaces.
- `features/` must never import `surfaces/` — this edge is rejected by
  `npm run check:architecture`.

## Junk-drawer test

- A first-order content capability? -> `features/`.
- Pure arrangement/navigation chrome? -> `shell/`.
- Product wiring (host-contract configuration, base layers)? -> `composition`
  composition.
- Dev-only probes and experimental fixtures? -> `tools/`, stories, or delete.
- Shipped troubleshooting actions and diagnostics? -> `help/diagnostics`, preserving their existing access gates.
# `client/features` — user-facing content capabilities (`@nucleum/features`)

Charter: the marquee things a user creates and manages. Each feature is a
self-contained capability reached from outside only through declared entry
points.

## Owners

`calendar`, `collections`, `focus`, `memory`, `records`, `spaces`.

## Belongs here

A cohesive content capability with its own UI, state, and logic.
`records` owns connected record actions and bulk mutations; shared-state
supplies their headless selection state and application-configured host.

## Import rules (enforced)

- May import `ui`, `shared-state`, `runtime`, `datafn`, and the application
  **shell** surface only.
- May **not** import `products` or application workflows outside the shell.
- Cross-feature imports must target a path declared in
  `tools/check/feature-entrypoints.json`; there is no barrel.

## Junk-drawer test

If the thing operates *across* features or is *about the app itself* — account
and billing, the command palette, the resource library/browser, settings,
onboarding, help — it is a **product surface** and belongs in the top-level

clipper transport events. `product` exposes the configured presentation host
consumed by surfaces without importing application composition.
`resources` owns headless resource state and host contracts; connected record
actions and bulk mutations live in `features/records`.

and no product-specific workflow. Concrete command *execution* lives in
`surfaces/commands`; final action registry assembly lives in `composition`.

`features`, or `products`.

- Pure infrastructure with no UI? -> `runtime/`.
- State owned by one feature? -> that feature.

  under a named owner above.

Charter: how the client talks to the outside world and computes, with no
presentation and no product workflow. It sits at the bottom and may be imported
by everyone, including extensions and workers that never load the full app.

## Owners

`account` (session state + transport), `audio`, `connectivity`, `embed`,
`inference`, `logging`, `os`, `context`.

## Belongs here

Transport, network authority, native/embed messaging, inference, audio decoding,
diagnostics, and the bare reactive state those need. Pure, low-dependency,
changes rarely.

## Never here (enforced)

Any import of `features`, `products`, `composition`, `surfaces`, the shell, `shared-state`,
or portable UI. Runtime is a leaf that others depend on, not the reverse.

## Junk-drawer test

- Has Svelte/DOM UI? -> not runtime.
- Coordinates a user-facing workflow (redirects, screens, prompts)? -> that
  workflow belongs in `surfaces` or a feature; keep only the primitive here.
  (Example: `account.store` state lives here; the sign-in workflow does not.)
# `client/ui` — portable, domain-free presentation (`@21n/ui`)

Charter: reusable UI that knows nothing about this product. It must be droppable
into any product or extension unchanged.

## Layers (import direction is one-way, top depends on bottom)

- `compositions` — compound UI built from primitives (charts, maps, breadcrumbs,
  nested lists, search controls, file presentation, duration/time inputs).
- `elements` — atomic controls and UI-only types.
- `actions` — generic DOM behaviors.
- `icons`, `illustrations`, `branding` — portable visual assets.
- `environment` — package-wide portable platform state.

`illustrations`, `branding`, `environment`, and `hosts` must never import

state, navigation, or infrastructure. A single current consumer is fine if reuse
is intended.

Any import, direct or transitive, of `composition`, `surfaces`, the shell, `products`,
`features`, `datafn`, `persistence`, `schema`, `shared-state`, or `runtime`.

# Type and contract ownership

Current type-placement contract. If this file disagrees with `docs/architecture/type-ownership-inventory.json` or `node tools/check/type-ownership.mjs`, the checker wins. Update the inventory in the same change that moves a type module.

Application, navigation, account, file, and command ownership lives in [client boundaries](client-boundaries.md). The TIDY-478 phase journal lives in [history/tidy-478-type-ownership.md](history/tidy-478-type-ownership.md).

## Conventions

Definitions stay beside their implementation unless independent consumers need a neutral contract. Feature contracts belong to the feature, and external callers use the public entries in `tools/check/feature-entrypoints.json`.

Portable UI controls own their structural prop and style types:

| Contract | Owner |
| --- | --- |
| Primitive prop and style types | `client/ui/elements` |
| Domain-neutral composition contracts | `client/ui/compositions` |
| Generic DOM-action contracts | `client/ui/actions` |
| Package-wide host contracts | `client/ui/hosts` |
| Portable platform state | `client/ui/environment` |
| Visual asset contracts | `client/ui/icons`, `client/ui/illustrations`, or `client/ui/branding` |

Those UI contracts do not derive from schema records, DataFn resources, runtime types, application actions, or state interfaces. Owning adapters translate domain models at the UI boundary.

| Contract | Owner |
| --- | --- |
| Keyboard and interaction mode | `client/ui/elements/keyboard` |
| Application action identifiers | `client/config` |
| Command host | `client/shared-state/commands` |
| Application events | `client/shared-state/events`. Focus and memory events live here. Clipper transport events live in `client/runtime/extensions`. |
| Resource panel and selection | `client/shared-state/resources` |
| Headless notification state | `client/shared-state/notifications` |
| Connected notification rendering | `client/shell/notifications` |
| Error recovery screens | `client/surfaces/help/errors` |
| Product menu contracts | `client/shell/navigation/app-menu.type.ts` |
| Browser ambient declarations | `client/ambient` |
| Cross-layer account, subscription, and legacy wire contracts | `schema` |
| Generated AuthFn and DataFn/Drizzle files | `services/account` generation scripts. Do not edit them by hand. |

`schema/account` owns profile and subscription wire data. Billing presentation fields stay in `client/surfaces/subscription`. `schema/legacy` owns the existing Surreal mutation, query, sync, resource-action, and store-data encodings. # Product composition (@nucleum/composition)

This workspace wires independently owned implementations into a running product.
It is not the default owner of connected components or workflows.

## Permanent owners

- root files: `configure-hosts.ts` registers hosts, `shortcuts.config.ts` supplies product shortcut defaults, `global-commands.ts` and `settings-actions.ts` assemble owner-defined actions, `SubAtomLogo.svelte` connects product identity to portable marks, and `AppLoadingView.svelte` and `ComponentResolver.svelte` connect startup and action presentation.
- layers: startup ordering, account access gating, connected user layout assembly, shell overlay mounting, product base layer wiring and telemetry consent/lifecycle wiring.
- chrome: product-connected snippets supplied to the independent shell, including native capture.

The root source files are an explicit allowlist in the architecture checker.
New root files or directories require an ownership decision and checker update.

## Responsibilities owned elsewhere

- shell/navigation and shell/layers: browser navigation, route decoding, route-driven layout, platform classes and viewport handling.
- shell/overlays and shell/modal: modal stacking, chrome and dismissal; composition registers the concrete action renderer and mounts the overlay layer.
- surfaces/settings and product settings owners: settings action definitions; composition preserves their final registry order.
- surfaces/library: mixed-resource rendering and bulk selection presentation; features/records owns record actions and bulk mutations.
- surfaces/account: OAuth, session hydration, extension login and environment-change sign-out.
- surfaces/subscription: plan reconciliation and native purchase outcomes.
- surfaces/settings/data-recovery: recovery decisions, UI, and DataFn import orchestration; persistence owns backup parsing and local storage mechanics.
- surfaces/settings/about: application-update workflow.
- surfaces/help: documentation, support, connected error recovery and shipped diagnostics.
- surfaces/sharing: permissions and public-link workflows.
- runtime: host detection, native message validation, service workers and log capture.
- shared-state/app-context, preferences and files: application metadata, timezone preferences and native file responses.
- ui/compositions: quick-access grids, hold-action presentation and point-map rendering.
- features/memory/maps: memory popup content and its map adapter.

Composition keeps lifecycle sequencing and supplies narrow callbacks to the
owning workflows. Do not move a large layer wholesale into another generic
controller, service, state or utilities directory. Do not add compatibility
re-exports at retired paths.

## Verification

Run npm run check:architecture, node tools/check/type-ownership.mjs, the product
compiler checks and relevant unit suites. Compiler/import success does not
prove browser, native purchase, legacy-data recovery or cloud behavior.

For the presentation-host and settings splits, manually verify account sign-in,
extension login, onboarding, branded loading, account navigation status,
library search and empty states, backup and restore, E2EE controls, and cache
actions on the Caddy HTTPS product hosts. Reopen settings and library surfaces
after writes to confirm persistent results.
# `client/shell` — application shell: arrangement and navigation (`@nucleum/shell`)

Charter: how the app is arranged and moved through, independent of what content
fills it. Pure "where things go and how you move", never "what a screen does".

## Owners

`navigation` (URL/history, resource navigation), `topNav`, `bottomNav`,
`leftPanel`, `rightPanel`, `trail`, `layers` (theme, metadata, embed),
`overlays`, `modal`, `paint` (page and
resource resolvers fed through the shared-state action renderer), `split views`,
`tabs`, `sync` and `notifications` chrome.

`navigation/NavigationLayout.svelte` owns route-driven arrangement and receives
connected nav snippets from application. `overlays/ModalLayer.svelte` owns the
overlay stack and resolves action content through the registered renderer.

## Belongs here

Anything that owns URL state, panel arrangement, tab/sidebar behavior, product
menus, or shell events. If removing it would not change what any single screen
does, only how screens are framed and reached, it belongs here.

## Not here

- Domain screens and workflows (account, library, settings, command) ->
  `surfaces/`.
- Portable domain-free UI -> `ui/`.
- Content capabilities -> `features/`.
- Sync scheduling -> `datafn/visibility-sync`; telemetry mechanics ->
  `runtime/telemetry`; consent/lifecycle wiring -> application layers;
  connected support -> `surfaces/help/support`.
- Application composition layers that wire the running product together
  (base/user layers, the action `ComponentResolver`, `AppLoadingView`, and the
  final settings action assembly) -> `composition/`.

## Dependency direction (enforced)

Shell is acyclic: it must not import `composition/`, `surfaces/`, or
`products/`, directly or transitively. Product navigation config enters through
