<script lang="ts">
  import { navigation } from "@nucleum/shell/navigation/navigation";

  import type { Snippet } from "svelte";
  import { page } from "$app/stores";
  import { resolveAuthSession } from "@nucleum/client/runtime/account/auth";
  import AppLoadingView from "@nucleum/composition/AppLoadingView.svelte";
  import Button from "@21n/ui/elements/button/Button.svelte";

  import { productData } from "@nucleum/products/product.resolver";
  import AuthGuard from "@nucleum/composition/layers/AuthGuard.svelte";
  import { postMessageToParent } from "@nucleum/client/runtime/embed/embed.utils";
  import { EmbedMessage } from "@nucleum/client/runtime/embed/embedMessage.enum";
  import { onMount } from "svelte";
  import AccountDebugInfo from "./AccountDebugInfo.svelte";
  let { children: pageChildren }: { children?: Snippet } = $props();
  let isEmbedTokenPresent = $state(false);
  const dev_isDebugAccountMode = false;
  onMount(() => {
    postMessageToParent(EmbedMessage.MOUNT);
    const token = localStorage.getItem("embedToken");
    isEmbedTokenPresent = token ? true : false;
  });

  type RouteAuthState =
    "authenticated" | "expired" | "signed-out" | "unavailable";

  const authPath = $derived($page.url.pathname);
  const hasAuthToken = $derived($page.url.searchParams.has("token"));
  const routeAuth = $derived({
    path: authPath,
    session: resolveRouteAuthState(hasAuthToken)
  });

  async function resolveRouteAuthState(
    hasToken: boolean
  ): Promise<RouteAuthState> {
    if (hasToken) return "authenticated";
    const resolution = await resolveAuthSession();
    if (
      resolution.status === "authenticated" ||
      resolution.status === "offline-only" ||
      resolution.status === "cached-cloud"
    ) {
      return "authenticated";
    }
    if (resolution.status === "expired") return "expired";
    if (resolution.status === "unavailable") return "unavailable";
    return "signed-out";
  }

  function goToAuthRoute(authState: RouteAuthState) {
    if (authState === "unavailable") {
      window.location.reload();
      return;
    }
    navigation.gotoPath("/account/login", {
      queryParams: authState === "expired" ? { msg: "expired" } : undefined
    });
  }
</script>

{#await routeAuth.session}
  <AppLoadingView />
{:then authState}
  {#if authState === "authenticated"}
    {#if dev_isDebugAccountMode}
      <AccountDebugInfo />
    {:else}
      <AuthGuard>
        {#snippet children(isLoggedIn)}
          {#if isLoggedIn}
            {@const ProductBase = productData.base}
            <ProductBase>
              {@render pageChildren?.()}
            </ProductBase>
          {/if}
        {/snippet}
      </AuthGuard>
    {/if}
  {:else}
    <div class="h-full flex flex-col justify-center items-center">
      {#if authState === "expired"}
        <div class="text-ass1 text-b2 mb-4">
          Your session has expired. Please login again.
        </div>
      {:else if authState === "unavailable"}
        <div class="text-ass1 text-b2 mb-4">
          Account service is unavailable. Please try again once it is running.
        </div>
      {/if}
      <div>Embed token: {isEmbedTokenPresent}</div>
      <Button
        label={authState === "unavailable" ? "Retry" : "Login/Signup"}
        onclick={() => {
          goToAuthRoute(authState);
        }}
      />
    </div>
  {/if}
{:catch error}
  <div class="h-full flex flex-col justify-center items-center">
    <div class="text-ass1 text-b2 mb-4">Authentication error</div>
    <Button
      label="Login/Signup"
      onclick={() => {
        navigation.gotoPath("/account/login");
      }}
    />
  </div>
{/await}

<script lang="ts">
  import { navigation } from "@nucleum/shell/navigation/navigation";

  import type { Snippet } from "svelte";
  import { page } from "$app/stores";
  import { resolveAuthSession } from "@nucleum/client/runtime/account/auth";
  import AppLoadingView from "@nucleum/composition/AppLoadingView.svelte";
  import Button from "@21n/ui/elements/button/Button.svelte";

  import { productData } from "@nucleum/products/product.resolver";
  import AuthGuard from "@nucleum/composition/layers/AuthGuard.svelte";
  import { postMessageToParent } from "@nucleum/client/runtime/embed/embed.utils";
  import { EmbedMessage } from "@nucleum/client/runtime/embed/embedMessage.enum";
  import { onMount } from "svelte";
  import AccountDebugInfo from "./AccountDebugInfo.svelte";
  let { children: pageChildren }: { children?: Snippet } = $props();
  let isEmbedTokenPresent = $state(false);
  const dev_isDebugAccountMode = false;
  onMount(() => {
    postMessageToParent(EmbedMessage.MOUNT);
    const token = localStorage.getItem("embedToken");
    isEmbedTokenPresent = token ? true : false;
  });

  type RouteAuthState =
    "authenticated" | "expired" | "signed-out" | "unavailable";

  const authPath = $derived($page.url.pathname);
  const hasAuthToken = $derived($page.url.searchParams.has("token"));
  const routeAuth = $derived({
    path: authPath,
    session: resolveRouteAuthState(hasAuthToken)
  });

  async function resolveRouteAuthState(
    hasToken: boolean
  ): Promise<RouteAuthState> {
    if (hasToken) return "authenticated";
    const resolution = await resolveAuthSession();
    if (
      resolution.status === "authenticated" ||
      resolution.status === "offline-only" ||
      resolution.status === "cached-cloud"
    ) {
      return "authenticated";
    }
    if (resolution.status === "expired") return "expired";
    if (resolution.status === "unavailable") return "unavailable";
    return "signed-out";
  }

  function goToAuthRoute(authState: RouteAuthState) {
    if (authState === "unavailable") {
      window.location.reload();
      return;
    }
    navigation.gotoPath("/account/login", {
      queryParams: authState === "expired" ? { msg: "expired" } : undefined
    });
  }
</script>

{#await routeAuth.session}
  <AppLoadingView />
{:then authState}
  {#if authState === "authenticated"}
    {#if dev_isDebugAccountMode}
      <AccountDebugInfo />
    {:else}
      <AuthGuard>
        {#snippet children(isLoggedIn)}
          {#if isLoggedIn}
            {@const ProductBase = productData.base}
            <ProductBase>
              {@render pageChildren?.()}
            </ProductBase>
          {/if}
        {/snippet}
      </AuthGuard>
    {/if}
  {:else}
    <div class="h-full flex flex-col justify-center items-center">
      {#if authState === "expired"}
        <div class="text-ass1 text-b2 mb-4">
          Your session has expired. Please login again.
        </div>
      {:else if authState === "unavailable"}
        <div class="text-ass1 text-b2 mb-4">
          Account service is unavailable. Please try again once it is running.
        </div>
      {/if}
      <div>Embed token: {isEmbedTokenPresent}</div>
      <Button
        label={authState === "unavailable" ? "Retry" : "Login/Signup"}
        onclick={() => {
          goToAuthRoute(authState);
        }}
      />
    </div>
  {/if}
{:catch error}
  <div class="h-full flex flex-col justify-center items-center">
    <div class="text-ass1 text-b2 mb-4">Authentication error</div>
    <Button
      label="Login/Signup"
      onclick={() => {
        navigation.gotoPath("/account/login");
      }}
    />
  </div>
{/await}

    62	## Closed edges
    63	
    64	`npm run check:architecture` enforces the matrix in `tools/check/client-dependency-matrix.json`, including type-only imports. These are the edges that are easy to miss from the matrix alone:
    65	
    66	- Features do not import products, surfaces, or composition. Shell is the only app-level layer they may use. Surfaces may compose features.
    67	- Surfaces do not import composition. Product fields arrive through `@nucleum/shared-state/product/surface-config-host`.
    68	- Shell does not import composition, surfaces, or products, directly or transitively. Product navigation arrives through `@nucleum/shared-state/product/product-config-host`.
    69	- Shared-state does not import composition, features, or products, directly or transitively, including through type-only imports.
    70	- DataFn and runtime do not import features, products, composition, shell, UI, or shared-state.
    71	- UI does not import application state, runtime, shell, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, or domain state, directly or transitively.
    72	- Inside UI, compositions may use elements, actions, icons, illustrations, branding, environment, and hosts. Those lower layers do not import compositions.
    73	- Composition calculations do not import the session singleton.
    74	- A caller outside a capability uses a source file listed in `tools/check/feature-entrypoints.json`. That list is the public surface, not a barrel. Additions are an explicit contract change. Package exports expose the same paths.
    75	
    76	Tests and stories are outside the production-source import gate. `client/ui` is one matrix owner; the lower-layer rule above is separate. The aggregate `client/package.json` is not a matrix owner.
    77	
    78	## Hosts
    79	
    80	Lower layers do not import composition to reach product behavior. `client/composition/configure-hosts.ts` runs from the base, user, and extension shells before presentation or command execution.
    81	
    82	| Contract | Installed by | Read by |
    83	| --- | --- | --- |
    84	| Command, action renderer, overlay, resource action, resource panel, record renderer, recents, shortcut, and product-presentation hosts | `configure-hosts.ts` | Shell, features, and surfaces |
    85	| `@21n/ui/hosts` and `@21n/ui/environment` | `configure-hosts.ts`, or the owning shell or feature adapter | Portable UI |
    86	| `product-config-host` | Composition | Shell |
    87	| `surface-config-host` | Composition | Surfaces |
    88	| Chrome snippets (brand, search, bulk edit, offline status, capture, profile) | `client/composition/chrome/` | Shell, through optional snippet props |
    89	| `persistence/logging-host` | Composition | Persistence |
    90	
    91	Shell and feature adapters pass view-specific props such as keyboard matching, time scales, and address resolution. Do not add a compatibility wrapper or a generic service locator.
    92	
    93	## Placement rules
    94	
    95	These rules are semantic. The import checker does not decide them.
    96	
    97	- A single current consumer does not make a composition feature-owned. Keep a domain-neutral composition in `client/ui/compositions` when future reuse is intentional.
    98	- A component moves to UI only when its public contract can be expressed without product or domain vocabulary. Neutral breadcrumbs and scroll containers live in UI. `client/shell/navigation/components/AppBreadcrumbs.svelte` turns resource and path metadata into those items. Sidebars, tabs, split views, panels, and trails stay in the shell while they own URL state, resource resolution, or product menus.
    99	- Product-aware branding that reads persistence or account identity stays in a named composition adapter, such as `client/composition/SubAtomLogo.svelte`, and composes portable marks through props.
   100	- Shared Markdown display owns portable parsing. Memory owns Markdown editing.
   101	- Account runtime state does not own file processing, deletion confirmation, or subscription workflows.
   102	- Do not recreate `client/utils`, `client/stores`, `client/state`, `client/commands`, `client/events`, `client/layout`, `client/branding`, `client/illustrations`, `client/icons`, `client/iconsV2`, or `client/application`. Do not add a catch-all `stores`, `state`, `shared`, or `core` directory.
   103	- When moving a module, update callers, feature exports, dependency declarations, and type-inventory destinations directly. Do not leave a compatibility re-export.

     7	## Conventions
     8	
     9	Definitions stay beside their implementation unless independent consumers need a neutral contract. Feature contracts belong to the feature, and external callers use the public entries in `tools/check/feature-entrypoints.json`.
    10	
    11	Portable UI controls own their structural prop and style types:
    12	
    13	| Contract | Owner |
    14	| --- | --- |
    15	| Primitive prop and style types | `client/ui/elements` |
    16	| Domain-neutral composition contracts | `client/ui/compositions` |
    17	| Generic DOM-action contracts | `client/ui/actions` |
    18	| Package-wide host contracts | `client/ui/hosts` |
    19	| Portable platform state | `client/ui/environment` |
    20	| Visual asset contracts | `client/ui/icons`, `client/ui/illustrations`, or `client/ui/branding` |
    21	
    22	Those UI contracts do not derive from schema records, DataFn resources, runtime types, application actions, or state interfaces. Owning adapters translate domain models at the UI boundary.
    23	
    24	| Contract | Owner |
    25	| --- | --- |
    26	| Keyboard and interaction mode | `client/ui/elements/keyboard` |
    27	| Application action identifiers | `client/config` |
    28	| Command host | `client/shared-state/commands` |
    29	| Application events | `client/shared-state/events`. Focus and memory events live here. Clipper transport events live in `client/runtime/extensions`. |
    30	| Resource panel and selection | `client/shared-state/resources` |
    31	| Headless notification state | `client/shared-state/notifications` |
    32	| Connected notification rendering | `client/shell/notifications` |
    33	| Error recovery screens | `client/surfaces/help/errors` |
    34	| Product menu contracts | `client/shell/navigation/app-menu.type.ts` |
    35	| Browser ambient declarations | `client/ambient` |
    36	| Cross-layer account, subscription, and legacy wire contracts | `schema` |
    37	| Generated AuthFn and DataFn/Drizzle files | `services/account` generation scripts. Do not edit them by hand. |
    38	
    39	`schema/account` owns profile and subscription wire data. Billing presentation fields stay in `client/surfaces/subscription`. `schema/legacy` owns the existing Surreal mutation, query, sync, resource-action, and store-data encodings. Do not derive those legacy shapes from current DataFn records. `schema/datafn.ts` derives resource names from `nucleumDatafnSchema`. Client `Resource`, `MetaResource`, and `Product` compose schema values with the Next overlay; backend callers import schema directly.
    40	
    41	Generic error codes are schema-owned. The default error message belongs to `client/shared-state/notifications`. Markdown validation belongs to memory. Responsive text truncation belongs to the text primitive. The legacy relay request contract lives in `server/common/relay/relay.type.ts` and imports only schema-owned resource and query contracts.
    42	
    43	Native transcription model identifiers and worker model identifiers are different protocols. Both live in `client/runtime/inference`, in separate modules, with their original enum values.
    44	
    45	The global `client/types` and `shared/types` packages are retired. Do not replace them with a catch-all types package or a compatibility export. Splits use a direct import to the actual owner.

    47	## Import and export rules
    48	
    49	Import interfaces and aliases with `import type` or a named `type` specifier. A runtime enum stays a value import. Do not re-export a moved definition from its former location. Public feature entries in `tools/check/feature-entrypoints.json` match the feature package exports. DataFn and schema expose their contracts directly.
    50	
    51	`npm run check:architecture` checks static imports, exports, dynamic imports, import types, CommonJS requires, and Vitest mock imports. It rejects production schema, shared, server, and service imports into client code, rejects every server-to-client import, and rejects retired package aliases. Historical specs and append-only `.conduct` reports may still name the old layout. Active guidance and configuration use the current owners.

    53	`node tools/check/type-ownership.mjs` checks every recorded destination in [type-ownership-inventory.json](type-ownership-inventory.json) and compares runtime enum declarations to that baseline.   const authPath = $derived($page.url.pathname);
  const hasAuthToken = $derived($page.url.searchParams.has("token"));
  const routeAuth = $derived({
    path: authPath,
    session: resolveRouteAuthState(hasAuthToken)
  });

  async function resolveRouteAuthState(
    hasToken: boolean
  ): Promise<RouteAuthState> {
    if (hasToken) return "authenticated";
    const resolution = await resolveAuthSession();
    if (
      resolution.status === "authenticated" ||
      resolution.status === "offline-only" ||
      resolution.status === "cached-cloud"
    ) {
      return "authenticated";
    }
    if (resolution.status === "expired") return "expired";
    if (resolution.status === "unavailable") return "unavailable";
    return "signed-out";
  }

  function goToAuthRoute(authState: RouteAuthState) {
    if (authState === "unavailable") {
      window.location.reload();
      return;
    }
    navigation.gotoPath("/account/login", {
      queryParams: authState === "expired" ? { msg: "expired" } : undefined
    });
  }
</script>

import fs from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";
import { execFileSync } from "node:child_process";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import { builtinModules } from "node:module";

const root = path.resolve(
  path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)),
  "../.."
);

/** Checks resolved source imports against declarations in their owning workspaces. */
export function checkWorkspaceDependencies(edges, externalImports = []) {
  const workspacePatterns = JSON.parse(
    fs.readFileSync(path.join(root, "package.json"), "utf8")
  ).workspaces.map(
    (pattern) =>
      new RegExp(
        `^${pattern.replace(/[.+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, "\\$&").replace(/\*/g, "[^/]+")}$`
      )
  );
  const manifests = execFileSync(
    "git",
    ["ls-files", "--cached", "--others", "--exclude-standard", "-z"],
    { cwd: root, encoding: "utf8" }
  )
    .split("\0")
    .filter(
      (file) =>
        file.endsWith("/package.json") &&
        !file.includes("node_modules/") &&
        fs.existsSync(path.join(root, file))
    )
    .map((file) => ({
      directory: path.posix.dirname(file),
      ...JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(root, file), "utf8"))
    }))
    .filter(
      (manifest) =>
        manifest.name &&
        workspacePatterns.some((pattern) => pattern.test(manifest.directory))
    )
    .sort((a, b) => b.directory.length - a.directory.length);
  const owner = (file) =>
    manifests.find((manifest) => file.startsWith(`${manifest.directory}/`));
  const failures = new Map();
  for (const edge of edges) {
    if (
      /\.(test|spec|stories)\./.test(edge.from) ||
      edge.from.includes("/tests/")
    )
      continue;
    const source = owner(edge.from);
    const target = owner(edge.to);
    if (!source || !target || source.name === target.name) continue;
    const declared = {
      ...source.dependencies,
      ...source.devDependencies,
      ...source.peerDependencies,
      ...source.optionalDependencies
    };
    if (!declared[target.name])
      failures.set(`${source.name}:${target.name}`, {
        ...edge,
        reason: `Undeclared workspace dependency: ${source.name} -> ${target.name}`
      });
  }
  for (const edge of externalImports) {
    if (
      /\.(test|spec|stories)\./.test(edge.from) ||
      edge.from.includes("/tests/") ||
      edge.to.startsWith(".") ||
      edge.to.startsWith("$") ||
      edge.to.startsWith("/") ||
      edge.to.includes(":") ||
      builtinModules.includes(edge.to)
    )
      continue;
    const source = owner(edge.from);
    if (!source) continue;
    const name = edge.to.startsWith("@")
      ? edge.to.split("/").slice(0, 2).join("/")
      : edge.to.split("/")[0];
    const declared = {
      ...source.dependencies,
      ...source.devDependencies,
      ...source.peerDependencies,
      ...source.optionalDependencies
    };
    if (!declared[name])
      failures.set(`${source.name}:${name}`, {
        ...edge,
        reason: `Undeclared external dependency: ${source.name} -> ${name}`
      });
  }
  return [...failures.values()];
}

## Belongs here

Presentation with credible cross-product reuse and **no** dependency on domain,
state, navigation, or infrastructure. A single current consumer is fine if reuse
is intended.

## Never here (enforced by `npm run check:architecture`)

Any import, direct or transitive, of `composition`, `surfaces`, the shell, `products`,
`features`, `datafn`, `persistence`, `schema`, `shared-state`, or `runtime`.

## Junk-drawer test

If it needs a store, navigation, a DataFn/domain type, or product branching, it
does **not** belong here. Feed those in through props or a `hosts` contract
configured by the owning application, shell, or feature layer.
   110	  configureHosts --> sharedHosts
   111	  configureHosts --> uiHosts
   112	  shell --> sharedHosts
   113	  features --> sharedHosts
   114	  surfaces --> sharedHosts
   115	  ui --> uiHosts
   116	```
   117	
   118	Product navigation reaches the shell only through `@nucleum/shared-state/product/product-config-host`. Brand, search, bulk edit, offline status, capture, and profile reach shell chrome as snippets from `client/composition/chrome/`. Persistence receives its logger through `persistence/logging-host`.
   119	
   120	## App component chain
   121	
   122	Nucleum, Memotron, and Pointron are thin SvelteKit hosts. Each app points its routes at `client/routes`. Product identity is `apps/<product>/src/local.ts`, which sets `base` to that product's layer.
   123	
   124	| App | Assembly | Product layer |
   125	| --- | --- | --- |
   126	| Nucleum | `apps/nucleus/src/local.ts` | `NucleusBaseLayer` |
   127	| Pointron | `apps/pointron/src/local.ts` | `PointronBaseLayer` |
   128	| Memotron | `apps/memotron/src/local.ts` | `MemotronBaseLayer` |
   129	
   130	Timear does not use this chain. Its routes live under `apps/timear/src/routes`.
   131	
   132	```mermaid
   133	flowchart TD
   134	  rootLayout["routes/+layout.svelte"]
   135	  baseLayer["BaseLayer"]
   136	  themeLayer["ThemeLayer"]
   137	  appGroup["routes/(app)/+layout.svelte"]
   138	  authGuard["AuthGuard"]
   139	  productBase["productData.base"]
   140	  userBase["UserBaseLayer"]
   141	  userLayout["UserLayout"]
   142	  navLayout["NavigationLayout"]
   143	  chrome["WiredLeftNav and WiredTopNav"]
   144	  painter["PagePainterV2"]
   145	  resolver["ComponentResolver"]
   146	  accountLayout["AccountLayout"]
   147	
   148	  rootLayout --> baseLayer --> themeLayer
   149	  themeLayer --> appGroup --> authGuard --> productBase
   150	  productBase --> userBase --> userLayout --> navLayout
   151	  navLayout --> chrome
   152	  navLayout --> painter --> resolver
   153	  themeLayer --> accountLayout
   154	```
   155	
   156	`BaseLayer` boots the shared app: version, account session, launch context, command registry, service worker, then connectivity. `configure-hosts.ts` is imported before children render.
   157	
   158	`AuthGuard` checks the product plan, sends an unbootstrapped cloud user to `/bootstrap`, and completes extension login. It then mounts `productData.base`.
   159	
   160	`UserBaseLayer` initializes DataFn and legacy recovery. It renders `UserLayout` only after `isBaseLoaded` and `isLocalLoaded`. Until then it shows `AppLoadingView` or the recovery gate. After load it also mounts `ModalLayer`, `ShortcutRunner`, and Intercom.
   161	
   162	`NavigationLayout` is the shell: left nav, top nav, split view, right panel, bottom nav, and trail. `PagePainterV2` maps the URL to an action. The action-renderer host is `ComponentResolver`, which renders that action's component. Panels, modals, and resource pages use the same resolver.
   163	
   164	Account routes (`client/routes/account`) stop at `AccountLayout` from `client/surfaces/account`. They do not mount the product base layer.

content.text:
**Mostly yes for the client’s structure, but a few details are inaccurate, and the map is not a complete picture of the system’s dependencies.**

The dependency-map table exactly matches the enforced matrix. All 146 public feature entries match package exports, and recorded current package names match manifests. Fresh checks passed: **11,554 resolved imports, zero architecture violations**, and all **383 type dispositions**.

These documentation leftovers remain:

| Issue | Correction needed |
|---|---|
| Both ownership docs say “the checker wins.” | Limit that to enforced import policy. The constitution and semantic ownership rules remain authoritative; the checker cannot establish correct ownership. |
| [Client boundaries](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:76) says stories are excluded. | The architecture gate includes 27 story files. Only the workspace-dependency check excludes stories. |
| [Type ownership](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/docs/architecture/type-ownership.md:51) says every server-to-client import is rejected. | Tests are excluded from that boundary rule; several server tests still import client Resource definitions. |
| UI environment is described as viewport/presentation measurements. | It also owns portable platform, appearance, debug, logging, haptic and asset-resolution contracts. The UI README’s blanket prohibition on stores needs the same qualification. |
| [The component chain](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/docs/architecture/client-dependency-map.md:160) says overlays, shortcuts and Intercom mount after loading. | Overlays and shortcuts require only `isBaseLoaded`; Intercom is outside the loading gate. |

The feature and shared-state READMEs also omit permitted dependencies while describing their lists as exhaustive.

**I think the architecture’s direction is good.** Portable UI, named state owners, cross-feature surfaces, a separate shell, and a narrow composition root give the code understandable homes. Host contracts and injected chrome successfully remove upward imports. I would keep this structure.

The next improvements should address these concrete weaknesses:

- **Finish semantic ownership cleanup.** [App context](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/shared-state/app-context/app.store.ts:22) still owns calendar selection (`selectedTimePeriod`), support configuration (`intercomId`), and a separate touch-device store populated by calendar code. `leftThresholdCrossedStore` has no callers. These belong with their existing semantic owners or should be removed when unused.
- **Reduce state-module cycles.** I found five cycle groups among value imports. Prioritize navigation↔tabs and analytics store↔analytics helpers. Recursive Markdown rendering may be intentional and deserves separate treatment.
- **Distinguish owner, workspace and observed graphs.** The permitted owner graph is acyclic, but `@nucleum/client` has mutual manifest dependencies with seven client packages, partly through peers. The current map documents its exclusion, but readers should not infer that the workspace graph is also acyclic.
- **Make host lifetime explicit.** Registration currently happens through module-import side effects, including an undisposed context subscription. Explicit installation and disposal would make isolated mounts, tests and reloads easier to reason about.
- **Generate the dependency table and add a system data-flow diagram.** Keep ownership prose handwritten. Add the client DataFn → account service → database/search/lookup paths, with legacy persistence and recovery boundaries.

The earlier Settings findings also remain documented: modal selection dismisses the overlay, and constrained landscape panels suppress detail content. The relevant source conditions remain; I did not repeat browser QA during this audit.

My priority order would be **documentation accuracy, semantic ownership leftovers, state cycles, then lifecycle and graph tooling**. This audit was read-only.
